<Rep. Maxine Waters, Rep. Brad Sherman, Rep. Stephen F. Lynch, Rep. Bill Foster, Rep. Joyce Beatty, Rep. Rashida Tlaib, Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia, Rep. Cleo Fields>: This bill would restrict and harm the SEC's mission of investor protection and capital formation. Among its provisions, this bill makes it harder for the SEC to help market participants comply with the law by requiring staff guidance and interpretive releases to meet the heightened procedural requirements of formal rulemakings, including by requiring staff to conduct cost-benefit analyses and notice-and-comment. For formal rulemakings, this bill adds an onerous step to the rulemaking process by requiring the SEC to continuously evaluate the cumulative impact of new regulations, diverting scarce resources to rules that have already been promulgated and inhibiting the ability of the SEC to consider and finalize new rules. The bill also dismantles, and moves the functions of, the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) to the SEC, exposing what have traditionally been nonpartisan audit, ethics, and quality control standards to the political whims of the Commission.
Democrats offered two amendments during mark-up of this bill. Ranking Member Waters offered an amendment to remove the problematic provisions of the bill that harm SEC's ability to protect investors, narrowing the bill to: require the SEC Chair testify semiannually; require GAO to audit SEC's IT infrastructure and data handling practices; and requiring 60-day notice-and-comment periods for most SEC rulemakings and an expedited 30-day comment period if the SEC determines risk of imminent investor harm. Rep. Lynch offered an amendment that would require SEC staff, when conducting cost-benefit analysis, to consider the impact a proposal would have on digital asset market infrastructure as well as financial market participants that use AI. Additionally, it would also require any cost-benefit analysis to look at a proposal's effects on investors and market integrity caused by the use of AI. Republicans rejected both amendments.
The bill is opposed by Americans for Financial Reform, Consumer Federation of America, and Public Citizen.
For these reasons, we oppose H.R. 9329.
Sincerely,
Maxine Waters,
Ranking Member.
Brad Sherman,
Stephen F. Lynch,
Bill Foster,
Joyce Beatty,
Rashida Tlaib,
Sylvia R. Garcia,
Cleo Fields,
Members of Congress.
